source_note: Web-verified research on British colonial looting episodes excluding Benin 1897: Maqdala 1868, Omdurman 1898, Asante 1874/1896/1900, Anglo-Zulu War 1879, Great Zimbabwe, Nigeria beyond Benin (Sokoto 1903, Aro 1901-02, Ife 1910), Uganda/Kenya. Key sources: BM contested-objects pages, V&A Asante/Ethiopia pages, AFROMET/Pankhurst, Patrick Watt (BJMH 2023), NMS 'Baggage and Belonging' regimental catalogues. Unverified seeds documented here: Fortnum & Mason (no source found — dropped); 'Christie's 1874 Asante sale' unconfirmed (documented 1874 dispersals are the Cape Coast prize auction, the Garrard sale, and Crown Agents sales).

actors.name: Richard Rivington Holmes
actors.role: British Museum agent embedded with the 1868 expedition; principal buyer at the prize auction; personal looter
actors.why_flag: BM's own provenance page documents he bought 13 objects at the Delanta Plain prize auction, took further objects during the looting (incl. Empress Tiruwork Wube's necklace), bought the gold crown and chalice (now V&A) from a soldier, and privately kept the Kwer'ata Re'esu icon. Appearance in an Ethiopian object's provenance is a documented association — review signal, not proof.

actors.name: Robert Napier
actors.role: Commander, 1868 Abyssinian Expedition; ordered loot collected for the prize auction; purchaser and distributor of loot
actors.why_flag: BM page: objects 'purchased at the auction of loot from Maqdala by Robert Napier' entered the BM via the Secretary of State for India; AFROMET documents he ordered loot collected for auction and later presented Maqdala manuscripts to Vienna, Berlin and Paris.

actors.name: Tristram Speedy
actors.role: Officer/collector on the 1868 expedition; guardian of Prince Alemayehu
actors.why_flag: BM page: 'Further items have come to the Museum from the collection of Captain Speedy... Some of the objects from his collection may have been taken from Maqdala or acquired during the Campaign,' with imprecise documentation. 'Ex-Speedy' provenance warrants review, including the items that entered via his widow Cornelia Mary Speedy (a recurring BM acquisition-name line for the same collection); some items were acquired on other visits.

actors.name: Bernard Quaritch
actors.role: London antiquarian bookseller; resold Maqdala manuscripts
actors.why_flag: Documented as the dealer through whom Maqdala manuscripts bought by officers at the loot auction were dispersed; Lady Meux bought her Maqdala manuscripts through Quaritch, outbidding the British Museum. Quaritch in an Ethiopian manuscript provenance is a review signal.
actors.source: Who was the Good Lady Meux? — https://tigraionline.com/articles/article11026.html

actors.name: Colonel Frazer (Maqdala 1868)
actors.role: Officer; major buyer at the Dalanta prize auction for a regimental mess
actors.why_flag: Pankhurst/AFROMET, citing Stanley: at the Dalanta auction 'Colonel Frazer, buying for a regimental mess, ran [Holmes] hard.' Regimental-mess purchases from this auction later surface in regimental museums. Surname ambiguous — match only with Maqdala context.

actors.name: Lady Valerie Meux
actors.role: Private collector of Maqdala manuscripts
actors.why_flag: Held the most famous private collection of Maqdala manuscripts (via Quaritch); her 1910 bequest to Emperor Menilek was overturned and the manuscripts dispersed. 'Ex-Meux' provenance on Ethiopian manuscripts is a strong review signal.

actors.name: Ernest Alfred Wallis Budge
actors.role: BM keeper/scholar associated with dispersed Maqdala manuscripts (Meux facsimiles)
actors.why_flag: AFROMET documents Budge translated/published Lady Meux's Maqdala manuscripts; his name attached to an Ethiopian manuscript can indicate the Meux/Maqdala line. Association-level signal only.

actors.name: William Simpson (war artist)
actors.role: ILN special artist on the 1868 expedition; acquired Ethiopian objects later given to the V&A
actors.why_flag: Covered the expedition and observed the looted royal quarters; acquired Ethiopian items that entered the V&A. Documented as purchases/gifts rather than loot — expedition-associated provenance still merits review at lower severity.

actors.name: Stafford Northcote
actors.role: Secretary of State for India; official conduit transferring Maqdala loot to the BM
actors.why_flag: BM page: Maqdala regalia, tabots and 300+ manuscripts purchased by Napier entered the BM/BL 'through the Secretary of State for India, Sir Stafford Northcote, in 1868.' 'Donated by the Secretary of State for India, 1868' in a record is a direct Maqdala flag.

actors.name: Garnet Wolseley
actors.role: Commander, 1873-74 Asante expedition (ordered palace stripped; appointed prize agents); commander in Zululand 1879
actors.why_flag: V&A: 'Wolseley ordered troops to gather as much of the royal regalia as possible and then destroy the royal palace' and 'appointed three prize agents'. The Witness documents an artifact looted from Ondini 'sent by Sir Garnet Wolseley to Queen Victoria'.

actors.name: Redvers Buller
actors.role: Intelligence officer and prize agent at Kumasi, February 1874
actors.why_flag: Watt (BJMH 2023): 'Among the prize agents were Captain Redvers Buller, the intelligence officer on the staff...'; also documented receiving an ntoa belt later displayed at NMS.

actors.name: Henry Dugdale
actors.role: Prize agent at Kumasi, 1874 (Rifle Brigade)
actors.why_flag: Named by Watt (BJMH 2023) as one of the three prize agents who selected the most valuable property in the Kumasi royal palace for the prize auction.

actors.name: Lieutenant Maclean (Naval Brigade, Kumasi 1874)
actors.role: Prize agent at Kumasi, 1874 (Naval Brigade)
actors.why_flag: Named by Watt (BJMH 2023) as the third Kumasi prize agent. Surname common — flag only with 1874 Asante context.

actors.name: Marie-Joseph Bonnat
actors.role: French trader who assisted the Kumasi prize agents, 1874
actors.why_flag: Watt (BJMH 2023): prize agents were 'assisted by Andooa, the leader of the Elmina people, and Marie-Joseph Bonnat, a French trader' in selecting palace property for the prize sale.

actors.name: Melton Prior
actors.role: ILN war correspondent; self-documented taker in the Kumasi palace, 1874
actors.why_flag: Watt (BJMH 2023) quotes Prior's own account of entering the royal bedchamber before the prize agents and taking gold slipper buckles to make 'a handsome brooch for my wife in England'.

actors.name: Henry Wood (10th Hussars, 1874)
actors.role: Courier who presented Wolseley's Asante trophies at Windsor, March 1874
actors.why_flag: Watt (BJMH 2023) documents Lt Henry Wood of the 10th Royal Hussars bringing campaign gifts/trophies to Windsor Castle on 10 March 1874 — a conduit into royal/private holdings. Common name — flag only with 1874 context.

actors.name: Serjeant Pearce (Asante 1874)
actors.role: Soldier who sold Asante jewellery and a goldweight to the South Kensington Museum, 1874
actors.why_flag: V&A: a week after the Garrard sale the museum 'bought two further items of jewellery and a copper-alloy goldweight from a Serjeant Pearce who either looted them himself without permission, or bought them at one of the sales.' Surname common — context required.

actors.name: Robert Baden-Powell
actors.role: Officer on the 1895-96 Asante expedition; supervised seizure of valuables in Kumasi
actors.why_flag: Restitution reporting documents that the gathering of gold and valuables in Kumasi in 1896 (incl. from the Bantama royal mausoleum precinct) was supervised by Baden-Powell; the BM records 1896-looted Prempeh I regalia in its collection.
actors.source: Modern Ghana — https://www.modernghana.com/news/310930/50/when-will-britain-return-looted-gold.html ; BM Asante Gold Regalia — https://www.britishmuseum.org/about-us/british-museum-story/contested-objects-collection/asante-gold-regalia

actors.name: Herbert Kitchener
actors.role: Commander at Omdurman 1898; ordered destruction/desecration of the Mahdi's tomb
actors.why_flag: Documented: the Mahdi's tomb destroyed on his orders, the body disinterred and beheaded, Kitchener retained the skull (later buried) and apologised to Queen Victoria; the Khalifa's Black Flag was sent to the Queen. Mahdist material with Kitchener/1898 provenance is flagged.
actors.source: The Mahdi's tomb — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mahdi%27s_tomb ; NAM Black Flag — https://collection.nam.ac.uk/detail.php?acc=1982-10-118-1

actors.name: Francis Reginald Wingate
actors.role: Intelligence chief of the Anglo-Egyptian conquest; collector of Mahdist documents and material
actors.why_flag: Durham University's Sudan Archive holds Wingate's papers including Mahdist documents formerly in his possession (some repurchased at auction in 1960 after dispersal). 'Ex-Wingate' provenance on Mahdist material is a documented review signal.

actors.name: John David Arthur Thomas Lloyd
aliases: Lieutenant J. D. A. T. Lloyd
actors.role: Lieutenant, 24th Regiment; serial collector/taker of Zulu material, 1879
actors.why_flag: NMS 'Baggage and Belonging' catalogue (Royal Welsh museum) records numerous Zulu necklaces, armlets, daggers, spoons, spearheads and a pipe 'collected'/'taken' by Lt J. D. A. T. Lloyd during the Anglo-Zulu War 1879.
actors.source: NMS Baggage and Belonging: Royal Welsh, Brecon — https://files.nms.ac.uk/production/Documents/Research/Baggage-and-Belonging-Catalogues/regimental-museum-of-the-royal-welsh-brecon.pdf

actors.name: Sergeant Major W. Hogan (24th Regiment)
actors.role: NCO who took a milk pail from Cetshwayo kaMpande's kraal, 1879
actors.why_flag: Catalogue entry: wooden milk pail 'found' at Cetshwayo kaMpande's kraal by Sgt Maj W. Hogan, 24th Regiment, 1879. Documented taking from the king's homestead.
actors.source: NMS Baggage and Belonging: Royal Welsh, Brecon — https://files.nms.ac.uk/production/Documents/Research/Baggage-and-Belonging-Catalogues/regimental-museum-of-the-royal-welsh-brecon.pdf

actors.name: William Dunbar (Major, 24th Regiment)
actors.role: Officer; took a Zulu shield at Rorke's Drift, 1879
actors.why_flag: Catalogue: Zulu shield 'taken' by Major William Dunbar at Rorke's Drift, with painted trophy label.
actors.source: NMS Baggage and Belonging: Royal Welsh, Brecon — https://files.nms.ac.uk/production/Documents/Research/Baggage-and-Belonging-Catalogues/regimental-museum-of-the-royal-welsh-brecon.pdf

actors.name: Henry Germain Mainwaring
actors.role: Officer; took a staff from Sihayo kaXonga's kraal, January 1879
actors.why_flag: Catalogue: staff 'taken from Sihayo kaXonga's kraal, 12th January 1879' by Lt H. G. Mainwaring, inscribed as trophy; also received a staff taken by Bromhead.
actors.source: NMS Baggage and Belonging: Royal Welsh, Brecon — https://files.nms.ac.uk/production/Documents/Research/Baggage-and-Belonging-Catalogues/regimental-museum-of-the-royal-welsh-brecon.pdf

actors.name: Gonville Bromhead
actors.role: Officer (Rorke's Drift); took Zulu staff and shield shaft, 1879
actors.why_flag: Catalogue: wooden staff 'taken' by Bromhead at Rorke's Drift (inscribed, later given to Mainwaring) and a Zulu shield shaft 'picked up at Rorke's Drift'.
actors.source: NMS Baggage and Belonging: Royal Welsh, Brecon — https://files.nms.ac.uk/production/Documents/Research/Baggage-and-Belonging-Catalogues/regimental-museum-of-the-royal-welsh-brecon.pdf

actors.name: Willi Posselt
actors.role: Hunter/trader; removed the first Great Zimbabwe soapstone bird, 1889; sold it to Rhodes
actors.why_flag: Documented in his own account: entered the sacred hill enclosure despite objections, hacked the best bird from its plinth under armed standoff, and sold it to Rhodes. Foundational red-flag name for Zimbabwe bird/soapstone provenance.

actors.name: Cecil Rhodes
actors.role: Financier; purchaser of Posselt's bird; commissioned Bent's excavation; behind the Ancient Ruins concession
actors.why_flag: Bought the first looted Zimbabwe bird (Groote Schuur; returned to Zimbabwe only in 2026); commissioned the 1891 Bent investigation after the BSAC invasion; gave Neal's Ancient Ruins Company its commission. Rhodes-linked provenance for southern African antiquities is a documented review signal.

actors.name: James Theodore Bent
actors.role: Antiquarian; excavated Great Zimbabwe 1891 for Rhodes/BSAC
actors.why_flag: Conducted the 1891 investigation of Great Zimbabwe commissioned by Rhodes following the BSAC invasion; documented the birds; his misattribution of the site fed the looting era. Bent provenance on Zimbabwe material merits review.

actors.name: W. G. Neal
actors.role: Operator of the Ancient Ruins Company (est. 1895)
actors.why_flag: Documented as running the Ancient Ruins Company under a Rhodes commission, stripping gold and artefacts from Great Zimbabwe and 50+ other sites (tens of kg of ancient gold melted/sold), destroying archaeology; co-author with R. N. Hall of 'The Ancient Ruins of Rhodesia'. Any Neal/Ancient Ruins provenance is a red flag.

actors.name: Richard Nicklin Hall
actors.role: First curator of Great Zimbabwe (from 1902); removed deposits; recovered further birds
actors.why_flag: Documented as the early curator whose clearance 'excavations' destroyed stratified deposits and who recovered two more birds; co-wrote the Neal/Hall volumes cataloguing extracted material. Use full name — bare 'Hall' is too common.

actors.name: Leo Frobenius
actors.role: German ethnographer; attempted removal of the Olokun head at Ife 1910; exported Ife terracottas; commercial Kasai expedition 1904-06
actors.why_flag: Documented: bought the sacred Olokun bronze head for a trivial sum in 1910, was forced by the British administration to give it up, and took Ife terracottas to Europe. Separately ran an explicitly commercial Kasai extraction expedition (1904-06, ~8,000 objects at 10 marks/piece for Hamburg; 1,827 more sold via Umlauff to the AMNH in 1912). Frobenius/DIAFE provenance warrants review.

actors.name: Charles Partridge
actors.role: District Commissioner, Southern Nigeria (1901-1915); collector during/after the Aro campaign era
actors.why_flag: Appointed DC in Southern Nigeria in 1901 (Obubura Hill, Ikot Ekpene etc.); donated his Eastern Nigeria collections (1903-13) to Ipswich Museum and the British Museum. Collections formed under military-occupation conditions — 'ex-Partridge' provenance merits review.

actors.name: Franklin Macaulay Gillespie
actors.role: Captain, Niger operations 1897-98; documented taker
actors.why_flag: NMS catalogue records Hausa bracelets/manillas and an iron knobkerrie described as 'taken' by Capt F. M. Gillespie during Niger operations 1897-8, now in the Royal Welsh museum.
actors.source: NMS Baggage and Belonging: Royal Welsh, Brecon — https://files.nms.ac.uk/production/Documents/Research/Baggage-and-Belonging-Catalogues/regimental-museum-of-the-royal-welsh-brecon.pdf

actors.name: Frederick Lugard
actors.role: High Commissioner of Northern Nigeria (1900-06); ordered the Kano-Sokoto campaign 1903; earlier commander in Uganda
actors.why_flag: The Sokoto Caliphate's restitution campaign concerns artefacts and manuscripts looted in the 1903 invasion under Lugard's administration; the BM's biography term (BIOG125735) links him to Nigerian and Kenyan objects in the collection. Documented association, review signal not proof.

actors.name: Henry Colvile
actors.role: Commander of the 1894 expedition against Bunyoro; took Omukama Kabalega's royal throne
actors.why_flag: Bunyoro Kingdom documents that Kabalega's royal stool/throne was taken by Col. Henry Colvile's forces after the battle of Rukungu in 1894; its whereabouts remain a live restitution question. Colvile provenance on Bunyoro material is a red flag.

actors.name: John Roscoe
actors.role: Missionary-anthropologist; major supplier of Ugandan objects to British museums (1890s-1920)
actors.why_flag: Museums Association: many of the 39 colonial-era Ugandan artefacts returned by Cambridge MAA in 2024 'were given to British museums by Reverend John Roscoe'; his Bunyoro collecting (1919-20) includes a royal stool at the Pitt Rivers Museum. Collecting under colonial rule — review signal, not proof of looting.

actors.name: Richard Meinertzhagen
actors.role: Colonial officer in British East Africa; killed Nandi leader Koitalel Arap Samoei (1905)
actors.why_flag: Documented in restitution reporting: Meinertzhagen shot Koitalel Arap Samoei in 1905; the body was decapitated and the head taken to London, with the skull and associated Nandi regalia still sought by Kenya. Meinertzhagen provenance on East African material is a documented red flag.

channels.name: Army prize system (prize committees, agents, auctions)
channels.type: military prize system (official loot collection and auction)
channels.why_flag: The formal mechanism converting loot to 'prize': Maqdala loot auctioned by an Army committee at Delanta Plain 20-21 April 1868; Kumasi palace property selected by appointed prize agents and auctioned at Cape Coast in 1874, with 'private spoils' also processed through the agents. Phrases like 'purchased at the prize sale/auction of loot' in provenance text are direct flags.

channels.name: R & S Garrard & Co
channels.why_flag: Appointed to sell the Asante indemnity gold; paid £11,000 for hundreds of items and sold them from their Haymarket showrooms in April 1874 (records lost in WWII); the BM bought 12 items directly from Garrard in 1874. Garrard 1874 provenance on West African gold is a primary red flag.
channels.source: V&A Asante gold — https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/a-history-of-asante-gold-at-the-vanda ; BM Asante Gold Regalia

channels.name: Phillips Brothers (goldsmiths)
channels.why_flag: BM: two Asante gold objects were purchased from the goldsmiths Phillips Brothers in 1891 — a documented secondary-market conduit for 1874-era Asante gold.

channels.name: Crown Agents for the Colonies
channels.why_flag: BM purchased 84 Asante gold objects via the Crown Agents in 1876 and a further 52 pieces (incl. regalia looted from Kumasi in 1896 and indemnity gold) from the Gold Coast government through the Crown Agents in 1900. 'Purchased from the Crown Agents' is a colonial-extraction provenance flag.

channels.name: Gold Coast colonial government transfers
channels.why_flag: BM: the Gold Coast government donated Asante objects in 1896 (some associated with the 1896 expedition) and sold the 1900 consignment of Prempeh I regalia and indemnity gold. Colonial-government donor lines on Asante material are review signals.

channels.name: India Office / Secretary of State for India transfers (1868)
channels.why_flag: The Maqdala expedition was launched through the India Office; Napier's purchases of loot and 300+ manuscripts entered the BM/BL 'through the Secretary of State for India' in 1868. This donor line in a record is a Maqdala flag.

channels.name: Royal gift/trophy channel (Queen Victoria presentations)
channels.why_flag: Six Maqdala manuscripts went to the Royal Library at Windsor; the Khalifa's Black Flag and Zulu royal items seized by Wolseley were sent to Queen Victoria; Wolseley's 1874 Asante gifts were presented at Windsor. 'Presented to the Queen/royal family' after these campaigns is a documented loot pathway. HIGH-VOLUME phrase — calibrate.
channels.source: AFROMET; NAM Black Flag; The Witness 2021

channels.name: Regimental messes and regimental museums
channels.why_flag: Officers bought loot for regimental messes (Colonel Frazer at Dalanta, 1868) and regiments retained trophies (Mahdi's tomb panel at the Museum of the Highlands; dozens of 'taken' Zulu, Niger and Sudan items at the Royal Welsh museum). 'By descent through the regiment' provenance is a systematic review signal. GENERIC — excluded from flat matching; use as KB context.
channels.source: AFROMET; Museum of the Highlands; NMS Baggage and Belonging

channels.name: Ancient Ruins Company (Rhodesia Ancient Ruins Ltd)
channels.why_flag: Founded 1895 under a Rhodes commission and run by W.G. Neal to exploit Rhodesian ruins; stripped gold and artefacts from Great Zimbabwe and 40-55+ other sites, melting much of it. Any object or gold with Ancient Ruins Company provenance is a red flag.

channels.name: British South Africa Company
channels.why_flag: Its 1890-91 invasion of Mashonaland created the conditions for the Bent excavation and the removal of the Zimbabwe birds and commercial ruin looting. BSAC-era provenance on Zimbabwean material merits review.

channels.name: Royal Niger Company (British episodes)
channels.why_flag: Documented in restitution reporting in connection with the violent conquest of the Sokoto region; company-era acquisitions from the Niger territories merit provenance review.

channels.name: Sudan Archive, Durham University (Wingate deposit)
channels.why_flag: Repository of Wingate's Mahdist manuscripts and papers (some dispersed at auction after his death, repurchased 1960). Comparable lines on Mahdist documents indicate 1898-conquest acquisition contexts. Holder, not culpable actor.

channels.name: National Army Museum (campaign-trophy holdings)
channels.type: museum holding channel for military loot
channels.why_flag: Holds Maqdala material, the Khalifa's Black Flag from Omdurman, Zulu War shields, and the Asante aya kese basin taken from the Bantama mausoleum in 1896. Holder-side channel — excluded from flat matching.
